findings.title: Device limit is bypassed because the local cache is populated before the DB write succeeds
findings.body: In `tagDeviceUI` the device's cache key is written (`a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})`, line 87) *before* `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs (line 93). With the new `return err` at line 147, `ErrDeviceLimitReached` now propagates through `TagDevice` into `Anonymous.Authenticate`, which returns `nil, err` and fails the request. But the cache entry set on line 87 is never removed on failure. On the next request from the same device (within the 29-minute cache TTL) `tagDeviceUI` hits the cache and returns nil without touching the DB, so `Authenticate` succeeds. Net effect: the limit only fails the very first request per device per 29 minutes and is trivially bypassed by reloading the page; furthermore, an expired device that `updateDevice` refuses to update still reaches the app on retry without ever being recorded, so it never counts toward the limit. The cache must only be populated after a successful write, and `ErrDeviceLimitReached` must not be masked by a cache hit.

findings.title: Count-then-insert device limiting is not atomic and allows exceeding the limit
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` first calls `CountDevices` and, only if `count < deviceLimit`, runs a separate INSERT ... ON CONFLICT. The count and the insert are independent statements with no transaction, lock, or conditional insert. Under concurrency, two first-time requests from different new devices can both observe `count < deviceLimit` and both insert, so the number of tracked devices exceeds the configured `device_limit`. Because tagging now runs synchronously on the authentication path, this race is easy to trigger with parallel browser sessions. The limit needs to be enforced atomically (e.g. a single conditional insert that also checks the count, or serialization via a lock), otherwise the configured limit is only advisory.

findings.title: Zero affected rows is conflated with 'device limit reached', producing false limit errors
findings.body: `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` whenever the UPDATE affects 0 rows. Zero rows means 'no row matched the WHERE clause', which also happens for legitimate cases that are not a limit breach: (a) a device that already exists but has not been updated in the last 30 days is excluded from `CountDevices` but its old `updated_at` is outside the `BETWEEN now-30d AND now+1m` window, so it can never be re-activated while the store is at capacity and is incorrectly reported as 'limit reached'; (b) on MySQL, `RowsAffected` reports *changed* rows, so if client_ip/user_agent are unchanged and `updated_at` is truncated to the same value the row matches but 0 rows are reported, yielding a false limit error. The error means 'could not refresh this device', not specifically 'limit reached', so callers and users are misled.

findings.title: Device-limit rejection is returned as a raw error and surfaces as an internal server error
findings.body: When `TagDevice` returns `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, `Authenticate` returns `nil, err`. That error is a plain `fmt.Errorf` with no HTTP status mapping, so the authn middleware has no way to translate it and the client over the limit receives an internal-server (500) response rather than a defined status such as 403/429. The raw 'device limit reached' string is also exposed. A dedicated typed/status error should be returned so the caller can respond with a meaningful status and message.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now performs a synchronous DB call using the request context
findings.body: The previous implementation tagged the device in a detached goroutine (`context.Background()` with a 2-minute timeout and a panic recovery). The new code calls `TagDevice(ctx, ...)` inline in `Authenticate` with the inbound request context. This adds a DB round-trip (a count plus an upsert) to the anonymous auth path, makes tagging fail if the inbound request context is cancelled or short-lived, and removes the panic recovery so a panic in tagging now propagates into authentication. If synchronous enforcement is required, at least keep panic recovery and use a bounded/detached context rather than the raw request context.

findings.title: Provider signature changed without regenerating wire_gen.go
findings.body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` changed its dependency from `anonstore.AnonStore` to `db.DB`, and `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` now requires an extra `int64` argument for which there is no wire provider. `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` is registered through Grafana's wire dependency graph, and `pkg/server/wire_gen.go` is generated but committed. That file is not part of this PR, so it still calls the old signature and the build will fail to compile unless `wire_gen.go` (and any wire set referencing `ProvideAnonDBStore`) is regenerated.

findings.title: No test covers the primary enforcement path or the cache-driven bypass
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a brand-new device gets `ErrDeviceLimitReached` a single time; it does not assert that an existing, in-window device can still be successfully re-tagged while the store is at capacity (the main reason for `updateDevice`), nor does it exercise the end-to-end rejection through `Anonymous.Authenticate`. `impl_test.go` only runs with the default limit of 0. As a result, neither the retry-after-error bypass (cache set before write, see impl.go) nor the false-limit cases in `updateDevice` are caught by the tests.

findings.title: Frontend type allows undefined but backend always sends 0
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceLimit` is typed `number | undefined` here (and defaulted to `undefined` in `GrafanaBootConfig`), but the backend DTO field `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` has no `omitempty`, so the JSON always contains the key and it is `0` when the feature is unlimited. Consumers that test `=== undefined` to detect 'not configured' will never match; they must treat `0` (or `<= 0`) as unlimited. Either make the DTO field a pointer with `omitempty` or type it as `number` and document that 0 means unlimited.
